_note: Probe case for the consistency measurement. TAK-994 is excluded from the benchmark, so using it here burns no development or held-out case. Its citations are UNVERIFIED upstream (data/out/tak994.json) and that is acceptable for a stability measurement, which needs no answer key - it would NOT be acceptable in a scored result.
context: Narcolepsy type 1. Chronic oral dosing in otherwise healthy adults, so tolerance for a liver signal is low. Decision point: whether to advance toward first-in-human.

rules.name: Human relevance
rules.statement: Human-cell evidence defeats animal in vivo evidence when the question is human hepatotoxicity.

rules.name: Mechanistic proximity
rules.statement: Evidence that directly measures an adverse outcome pathway key event defeats evidence that only correlates with chemical structure.

rules.name: Exposure relevance
rules.statement: A positive finding at clinically relevant exposure defeats a negative finding whose exposure margin is unstated or untested at that range.

rules.name: Applicability domain
rules.statement: Evidence from a model operating outside its applicability domain is admitted with reduced weight, or excluded.

rules.name: Study reliability
rules.statement: Higher-reliability studies defeat lower-reliability ones at equal mechanistic relevance.

rules.name: Concordance
rules.statement: Independent sources agreeing raises confidence more than one source agreeing with itself.

absent.whatItBlocks: 4 of 6 findings assert SAFE with no established exposure margin (TAK-994:invivo_rodent, TAK-994:invivo_nonrodent, TAK-994:cytotox, TAK-994:transporter). Each rules out less than it appears to, and none can be distinguished from a result tested below the range that matters.
3 findings correlate rather than measure (TAK-994:invivo_rodent, TAK-994:invivo_nonrodent, TAK-994:qsar), so they evidence no mechanism in either direction.
